definition: a person or company that owns a home and rents it to others
example: I emailed my landlord about the broken heater, but he hasn't replied yet.

definition: a person who pays rent to live in a place
example: Tenants in this building must give one month's notice before moving out.

definition: to sign a legal contract for renting a home for a period of time
example: Before you sign a lease, read the section about pets and parking carefully.

definition: money paid to a landlord at the start of a rental, returned later if there is no damage
example: The landlord returned my full security deposit because the apartment was spotless.

definition: a rise in the amount of rent a tenant pays
example: BC limits the annual rent increase a landlord can charge for most rental units.

definition: basic services for a home such as electricity, heat, water and gas
vi: các tiện ích sinh hoạt (điện, nước, ga, sưởi)
example: The rent is $1,900 a month, and utilities are included except for internet.

definition: a formal request asking a building manager to fix something
vi: yêu cầu sửa chữa, bảo trì
example: I submitted a maintenance request online, but nobody has come to fix the leak.
collocations: follow up on a maintenance request

definition: to leave the home where you live and take your things with you
vi: dọn ra, chuyển đi (khỏi nơi ở)
example: We plan to move out at the end of June when our lease expires.

definition: to officially tell someone in advance that you will leave or end an agreement
vi: báo trước (việc dọn đi, chấm dứt hợp đồng thuê)
example: You must give notice in writing at least one full month before you leave the unit.

definition: a separate apartment on the lowest floor of a house, common in BC
vi: căn hộ tầng hầm (cho thuê riêng)
example: We rented a two-bedroom basement suite in Burnaby because it was cheaper than a condo.

definition: a monthly fee condo owners in BC pay for shared building costs
vi: phí quản lý chung cư (phí strata)
example: The strata fee covers snow removal, building insurance and the gym.

definition: a person or company hired to run a rental building for the owner
vi: người/công ty quản lý bất động sản
example: The property manager said the elevator would be repaired by Friday.

definition: a person who shares a home with you
vi: bạn cùng phòng, người ở ghép
example: Living with a roommate helped me save money during my first year in Vancouver.

definition: already containing furniture
example: The studio is fully furnished, so you only need to bring your clothes.

definition: having a lot of room or space
example: The townhouse has a spacious living room and a small backyard for the kids.

definition: uncomfortably small and crowded
example: Our old apartment felt cramped after the baby was born.

definition: an area of a town or city and the people who live there
example: We chose this neighbourhood because it has good schools and a quiet park.

definition: a report that someone is making too much noise
example: After a noise complaint from the unit below, we put rugs on our hardwood floors.

definition: work done to repair and improve a building
vi: sự cải tạo, sửa sang (nhà cửa)
example: The lobby will be closed during the renovation, so please use the side entrance.

definition: water escaping from a pipe, roof or appliance where it should not
example: A water leak from the upstairs bathroom damaged our kitchen ceiling.

definition: the removal of insects or animals such as mice from a building
vi: diệt côn trùng, kiểm soát sinh vật gây hại
example: The landlord called pest control after tenants reported mice in the laundry room.

definition: homes that people with low or average incomes can afford
example: The city council approved a plan to build 500 units of affordable housing near the SkyTrain.

definition: the first part of the price you pay when buying a home with a loan
example: It took us six years to save enough for a down payment on a condo.

definition: a home or room that is empty and available to rent
example: Vancouver's low vacancy rate makes it hard to find an apartment.

definition: to rent your rented home to another person for a time
vi: cho thuê lại (nhà mình đang thuê)
example: You need the landlord's written permission to sublet your apartment while you travel.

definition: a washer and dryer inside your own apartment
vi: máy giặt, máy sấy riêng trong căn hộ
example: I'm willing to pay a little more for a place with in-suite laundry.

definition: allowing or welcoming pets
example: It's hard to find a pet-friendly rental in this city if you have a large dog.

definition: close enough to walk to
vi: trong khoảng cách đi bộ được
example: The apartment is within walking distance of a grocery store and two bus stops.
collocations: within walking distance of the station

definition: to legally force someone to leave the home they rent
vi: đuổi (người thuê) ra khỏi nhà, cưỡng chế dọn đi
example: A landlord cannot evict a tenant without following the proper legal process.

definition: electrical machines used at home, such as a fridge or stove
example: All appliances in the kitchen were replaced last year, including the dishwasher.

definition: a time when a home for sale is open for anyone to visit
vi: buổi mở cửa cho xem nhà
example: We went to three open houses on Sunday, but none had enough parking.

definition: to move to a smaller home
example: After their children moved out, my parents decided to downsize to a two-bedroom condo.

definition: a person who owns the home they live in
vi: chủ sở hữu nhà, người có nhà riêng
example: As a first-time homeowner, I didn't expect so many maintenance costs.

definition: to repair or improve a place
example: We bought an older house and spent the summer fixing up the kitchen.

definition: useful features or services in a building or area, such as a gym or park
vi: tiện ích, tiện nghi (khu nhà, khu vực)
example: The building's amenities include a rooftop garden, a gym and bike storage.

definition: to start living in a new home
example: We're planning to move in on the first of the month, so we booked a truck for that morning.

definition: an advertisement for a home that is available to rent
example: The rental listing said utilities were included, but the landlord later asked us to pay for hydro.

definition: a small apartment with one main room for living and sleeping, plus a kitchen area and bathroom
example: A studio apartment near the SkyTrain is enough for me, since I live alone and work most of the day.

definition: a house that is joined to similar houses on one or both sides, often with two or three floors
example: We moved from a condo to a townhouse in Surrey so the kids could have a small backyard.

definition: a person whose job is to help people buy, sell or rent homes
vi: nhân viên môi giới bất động sản
example: Our realtor warned us that homes in this neighbourhood usually sell within a week.

definition: a device that makes a loud noise when it senses smoke
example: Please test the smoke detector in your unit once a month and tell the manager if it stops working.

definition: a small locked space in a building where residents can keep extra belongings
example: Each unit comes with one parking spot and a storage locker in the underground parkade.
collocations: a storage locker in the basement

definition: the official written contract between a landlord and a tenant
example: According to our tenancy agreement, the landlord is responsible for repairs to major appliances.
collocations: the terms of the tenancy agreement
a copy of the tenancy agreement

definition: a check of a rental unit's condition that the landlord and tenant do together at the start of a tenancy, usually on or just before move-in day
vi: kiểm tra tình trạng nhà khi dọn vào
example: During the move-in inspection, we took photos of every scratch on the floor so there would be no dispute later.

definition: the normal damage that happens to something when it is used over time
example: A few small marks on the walls are normal wear and tear, so the landlord shouldn't charge us for them.

definition: continuing one month at a time with no fixed end date
vi: theo từng tháng (không thời hạn cố định)
example: After the first year, our lease became month-to-month, which gives us more flexibility to move.

definition: a rental contract that lasts for a set period, such as one year
vi: hợp đồng thuê có thời hạn cố định
example: We signed a fixed-term lease for twelve months because the landlord offered a lower rent that way.
collocations: the end of a fixed-term lease

definition: a group of owners elected to manage the shared property and day-to-day business of a condo or townhouse complex for all the owners
example: The strata council voted to replace the old elevator, but some owners are unhappy about the cost.

definition: times of day, usually at night, when residents are expected to keep noise low
example: Our building's quiet hours start at 10 p.m., so please keep the music down after that.

definition: a part of a building that all residents share, such as the lobby, hallways or gym
example: Bikes are not allowed in the common areas, so please use the bike room on the ground floor.

definition: a soft green, grey or black growth that forms in damp places and can affect health
example: There's mould around the bathroom window again because the fan doesn't remove enough moisture.

definition: a pipe that is blocked so water cannot flow away
example: I submitted a request about the clogged drain in the kitchen sink, but nobody has come to fix it.

definition: in good enough condition that you can live there immediately without repairs
vi: có thể dọn vào ở ngay
example: The house is move-in ready, so we won't need to spend money on renovations right away.

definition: to do the work needed to fix something
example: The landlord plans to carry out repairs on the balcony next week, so we need to remove our plants.

definition: to have not paid all the rent that is owed by the due date
example: After losing his job, Daniel was behind on rent for two months and felt too embarrassed to tell his landlord.
collocations: be two months behind on rent

definition: the buying, selling and renting of homes in an area, and how prices change
example: The housing market in Metro Vancouver is so competitive that many young families move to the Fraser Valley.

definition: to become comfortable in a new home or place
vi: ổn định chỗ ở; quen dần với nơi mới
example: It took us a few months to settle in, but now we know all our neighbours by name.

definition: a home where several people rent rooms and share the kitchen or bathroom
example: Many international students choose shared accommodation because a whole apartment is too expensive.

definition: insurance that protects a renter's belongings and covers some damage they may cause
vi: bảo hiểm cho người thuê nhà
example: Our landlord requires every tenant to have tenant insurance in case of a fire or a flood.

definition: to become in bad condition because nobody has looked after it
vi: xuống cấp vì không được bảo trì
example: Older buildings can quickly fall into disrepair when owners stop paying for basic maintenance.
collocations: be allowed to fall into disrepair

definition: a disagreement between a landlord and a tenant, for example about repairs or a deposit
example: To avoid a tenancy dispute, keep copies of every email and receipt you send to your landlord.
collocations: a tenancy dispute over the deposit

definition: a non-profit housing community owned collectively by its members, who pay monthly housing charges instead of rent and share decisions
example: Living in a housing co-op means attending meetings and volunteering, but the monthly charges are often lower.
collocations: a waiting list for a housing co-op

definition: a house in poor condition that is sold cheaply because it needs a lot of repairs
vi: nhà cũ cần sửa chữa nhiều
example: We bought a fixer-upper in Nanaimo and have spent every weekend since then painting and replacing floors.

definition: a situation where several buyers keep offering more money for the same property
example: The bungalow was listed below market value, which started a bidding war among a dozen buyers.

definition: to become too big for something, or to need more than it can offer
vi: trở nên quá chật/không còn phù hợp
example: With a second baby on the way, we've outgrown our one-bedroom apartment.

definition: a person who is interested in renting a place and may become a tenant
vi: người có ý định thuê nhà
example: The property manager asks every prospective tenant for references from previous landlords.

definition: to take an amount away from a total
example: The landlord deducted the cost of carpet cleaning from our deposit without asking us first.

definition: built so that sound cannot easily pass through
example: The walls aren't very soundproof, so I can hear my neighbour's TV every evening.

definition: to officially finish a rental arrangement between a landlord and a tenant
vi: chấm dứt hợp đồng thuê nhà
example: If you want to end a tenancy early, check your agreement and talk to your landlord in writing.
collocations: the right to end a tenancy
a notice to end a tenancy

definition: a small, affordable home bought by people who are buying their first property
vi: căn nhà đầu tiên (giá vừa phải)
example: Starter homes have become hard to find in the Lower Mainland, so many couples rent for longer.

definition: needing little work or care to keep in good condition
vi: ít cần bảo trì, dễ chăm sóc
example: We chose a condo because it's low-maintenance; we don't have to mow a lawn or clear snow.

definition: how much money a home or piece of land is worth
example: Some residents worry that the new highway will lower property values in the area.

definition: old and in very bad condition because it has not been cared for
vi: đổ nát, xuống cấp nghiêm trọng
example: The dilapidated motel on Main Street will finally be torn down to make room for new rental housing.

definition: safe and good enough to live in
example: After the flood, the basement was not habitable until the walls and flooring were replaced.

definition: how attractive a house looks from the street
vi: vẻ hấp dẫn bên ngoài của ngôi nhà
example: Painting the front door and planting flowers can add curb appeal before you put your house on the market.

definition: so expensive that most people cannot afford it
vi: đắt đến mức không thể chi trả
example: For many young workers, buying a detached house in the city has become prohibitively expensive.

definition: in BC and some other provinces, a bill for the electricity used in a home (from "hydroelectric")
example: Our hydro bill almost doubled in January because we used the baseboard heaters every night.
